_provenance.generated_by: Quasispecies replicator-mutator model with single-peak fitness landscape
_provenance.data_origin: Analytical: Eigen error threshold mu_c = 1 - sigma^(-1/L). Steady-state master frequency x_m = (sigma*Q - 1)/(sigma - 1) where Q = (1-mu)^L.

_description: Tests Eigen's error threshold: the mutation rate above which self-replicating information is destroyed by noise. This is the most fundamental formulation of groundSpring's central question — when does signal survive in a noisy system?
_groundspring_question: At what mutation rate does noise (copying errors) destroy signal (heritable information)? The error threshold mu_c = ln(sigma)/L defines the boundary between information preservation and information death.
_cross_spring: wetSpring — microbial evolution; Exp 014 (drift vs selection). Dolson (2023) extends to origin-of-life context.

model._description: Single-peak fitness landscape: master sequence has fitness sigma, all mutants have fitness 1. Population of N individuals, genome length L, per-base mutation rate mu. Discrete-generation Wright-Fisher selection + independent per-base mutation.

analytical_predictions._description: Eigen (1971): error threshold at mu_c = 1 - sigma^(-1/L). Steady-state master frequency x_m = (sigma*Q - 1)/(sigma - 1) where Q = (1-mu)^L. For mu_c with sigma=10, L=100: mu_c ≈ 0.02276.
